'''Timothy P. Lodge''' (born 11 April 1954) is an American polymer scientist.

Lodge is a Regents Professor (2013–present),<ref name="CFP">{{cite web|url=http://www.chem.umn.edu/news/news.lasso?serial=572 |title=Department of Chemistry |publisher=Chem.umn.edu |date=2013-06-14 |access-date=2015-03-10}}</ref> an Institute of Technology Distinguished Professor (2004–present), and a Distinguished McKnight University Professor (2001–present)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scholarswalk.umn.edu/awards/mcknight/mcknight_distinguished.html |title=University of Minnesota: Scholars Walk |publisher=Scholarswalk.umn.edu |date=2015-01-23 |access-date=2015-03-10}}</ref> in the Department of Chemistry and the Department of Chemical Engineering and [[Materials science|Materials Science]] at the [[University of Minnesota]], [[twin cities|Twin Cities]], [[Minneapolis-Saint Paul]], Minnesota where he has been a faculty member since 1982. He served as the Editor-in-Chief of the [[American Chemical Society]] journal [[Macromolecules (journal)|''Macromolecules'']] for 17 years (2001–2017) and as the founding editor of ''[[ACS Macro Letters]]'' (2011–2018).<ref name="CFP"/>

He is recognized for his research in [[polymer science]], especially fundamental explorations of [[polymer]] chain dynamics in [[miscibility|miscible blends]], block polymers, multicompartment [[micelle]]s and polymers in [[ionic liquid]]s. According to ''Web of Science'', he has produced 331 published works that have been cited over 12,400 times, with an [[h-index]] of 62 as of April 6, 2014. He is also co-author, with Paul Hiemenz, of the textbook, ''Polymer Chemistry, 2nd edition.''<ref name="CFP"/>

==Background and personal life==
Timothy P. Lodge was born in Manchester, England, a son of Helen and [[Arthur S. Lodge]]. He moved permanently to the United States in 1968. He received his A. B. degree in applied mathematics from Harvard University in 1975.<ref name="TPL">{{cite web | url=http://www.chem.umn.edu/directory/faculty.lasso?serial=456 | title=Chemistry Faculty Profile Timothy P. Lodge | publisher=University of Minnesota | access-date=7 November 2015}}</ref> Working under the [[mentorship]] of Professor John Schrag at the University of Wisconsin, Madison, Lodge received his Ph.D. in chemistry in 1980.<ref name="TPL"/> His dissertation was titled, "Oscillatory Flow Birefringence of Dilute Polymer Solutions:  Concentration Dependence and High Frequency Behavior." Upon graduation, Lodge collaborated with Dr. Charles Han as a National Research Council Postdoctoral Associate at the National Bureau of Standards (now the National Institute of Standards and Technology).<ref name="CFP"/> Lodge and his wife have two children.{{citation needed|date=November 2015}}

==Contributions to polymer science==
Lodge is internationally recognized for his seminal contributions in numerous areas of polymer science.<ref name="CFP"/>  The focus of his work has been on achieving a molecular-level understanding of polymer structure and dynamics in multicomponent systems and mixtures, and to understand how these are affected by the thermodynamic interactions amongst the components.

'''Polymer chain dynamics:''' Lodge's early work focused on the chain dynamics of polymers in solution and in miscible blends.  In particular, Lodge and McLeish (2000) discussed the effect of local composition on the dynamics of polymers in a miscible blend.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Lodge | first1=Timothy P. | last2=McLeish | first2=Thomas C. B. | title=Self-Concentrations and Effective Glass Transition Temperatures in Polymer Blends | journal=Macromolecules | publisher=American Chemical Society (ACS) | volume=33 | issue=14 | year=2000 | issn=0024-9297 | doi=10.1021/ma9921706 | pages=5278–5284| bibcode=2000MaMol..33.5278L }}</ref>  Their model was based on two simple assumptions.  First, that dynamic heterogeneity occurs over a length scale on the order of a [[Kuhn length]] of the chain.  Second, that each polymer in the blend experiences a 'self-concentration' that is higher than the bulk (average) composition, due to chain connectivity over this length scale.  The impact is that the local dynamics of the two polymers in the blend may exhibit different dependencies on temperature and overall composition due to differences in local composition.  This leads to a breakdown in [[time-temperature superposition]],<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Haley | first1=Jeffrey C. | last2=Lodge | first2=Timothy P. | title=Failure of time-temperature superposition in dilute miscible polymer blends | journal=Colloid & Polymer Science | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=282 | issue=8 | date=2004-06-01 | issn=0303-402X | doi=10.1007/s00396-004-1092-5 | pages=793–801| s2cid=96272557 }}</ref> and the appearance of two distinct [[glass transition]] temperatures in the mixture.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Savin | first1=Daniel A. | last2=Larson | first2=Anne M. | last3=Lodge | first3=Timothy P. | title=Effect of composition on the width of the calorimetric glass transition in polymer-solvent and solvent-solvent mixtures | journal=Journal of Polymer Science Part B: Polymer Physics | publisher=Wiley | volume=42 | issue=7 | year=2004 | issn=0887-6266 | doi=10.1002/polb.10776 | pages=1155–1163| bibcode=2004JPoSB..42.1155S }}</ref><ref name="autogenerated1998">{{cite journal | last1=Hanley | first1=Kenneth J. | last2=Lodge | first2=Timothy P. | title=Effect of dilution on a block copolymer in the complex phase window | journal=Journal of Polymer Science Part B: Polymer Physics | publisher=Wiley | volume=36 | issue=17 | year=1998 | issn=0887-6266 | doi=10.1002/(sici)1099-0488(199812)36:17<3101::aid-polb10>3.0.co;2-x | pages=3101–3113| bibcode=1998JPoSB..36.3101H }}</ref>

'''Block copolymer solutions:''' Lodge's research group has maintained long-standing interest in the self-assembly of block [[copolymers]] in solutions. Studying the phase behavior of polystyrene-block-polyisoprene in solvents of varying selectivity, the concept of phase trajectories was introduced to explain the phase sequences observed as a function of concentration in neutral and selective solvents connecting the solution behavior to that seen in block copolymer melts.<ref name="autogenerated1998"/><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Hanley | first1=Kenneth J. | last2=Lodge | first2=Timothy P. | last3=Huang | first3=Ching-I | title=Phase Behavior of a Block Copolymer in Solvents of Varying Selectivity | journal=Macromolecules | publisher=American Chemical Society (ACS) | volume=33 | issue=16 | year=2000 | issn=0024-9297 | doi=10.1021/ma000318b | pages=5918–5931| bibcode=2000MaMol..33.5918H | url=http://ntur.lib.ntu.edu.tw/bitstream/246246/127907/1/03.pdf }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Lodge | first1=Timothy P. | last2=Pudil | first2=Bryant | last3=Hanley | first3=Kenneth J. | title=The Full Phase Behavior for Block Copolymers in Solvents of Varying Selectivity | journal=Macromolecules | publisher=American Chemical Society (ACS) | volume=35 | issue=12 | year=2002 | issn=0024-9297 | doi=10.1021/ma0200975 | pages=4707–4717| bibcode=2002MaMol..35.4707L }}</ref> From this foundation, the [[thermodynamics]] and [[Chemical kinetics|kinetics]] of [[Polymorphism '''Miktoarm Star Polymers:''' In 2004, Lodge published the seminal paper on the self-assembly of miktoarm star terpolymers in solution;<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Li | first1=Z. |last2=Kesselman|first2=E.|last3=Talmon|first3= Y.|last4= Hillmyer|first4= M. A.|last5= Lodge|first5= T. P.| title=Multicompartment Micelles from ABC Miktoarm Stars in Water | journal=Science | publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) | volume=306 | issue=5693 | date=2004-10-01 | issn=0036-8075 | doi=10.1126/science.1103350 | pages=98–101| pmid=15459387 | bibcode=2004Sci...306...98L | s2cid=262629683 }}</ref> a paper that has been cited over 600 times.<ref name="CFP"/>  Using ABC miktoarm star polymers the first example of multicomponent block copolymer micelles was shown, driven by the mutual incompatibility of the [[Hydrophile|hydrophilic]] A and hydrophobic B and C blocks.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Li | first1=Zhibo | last2=Hillmyer | first2=Marc A. | last3=Lodge | first3=Timothy P. | title=Morphologies of Multicompartment Micelles Formed by ABC Miktoarm Star Terpolymers | journal=Langmuir | publisher=American Chemical Society (ACS) | volume=22 | issue=22 | year=2006 | issn=0743-7463 | doi=10.1021/la0620051 | pages=9409–9417| pmid=17042562 }}</ref> In a subsequent paper the simultaneous, segregated storage of two different [[chromophore]]s in the different micelle domains was demonstrated, offering potential for use in chemical delivery in fields such as pharmaceuticals, personal care products, and foodstuffs.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Lodge | first1=Timothy P. | last2=Rasdal | first2=April | last3=Li | first3=Zhibo | last4=Hillmyer | first4=Marc A. | title=Simultaneous, Segregated Storage of Two Agents in a Multicompartment Micelle | journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society | publisher=American Chemical Society (ACS) | volume=127 | issue=50 | year=2005 | issn=0002-7863 | doi=10.1021/ja056841t | pages=17608–17609| pmid=16351082 | bibcode=2005JAChS.12717608L }}</ref>

'''Polymers in Ionic Liquids:'''  Lodge's recent work has focused on the self-assembly of block copolymers in [[ionic liquids]].<ref>{{cite journal | last=Lodge | first=T. P. | title=Materials Science: A Unique Platform for Materials Design | journal=Science | publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) | volume=321 | issue=5885 | date=2008-07-04 | issn=0036-8075 | doi=10.1126/science.1159652 | pages=50–51| pmid=18599764 | s2cid=206513712 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=He | first1=Yiyong | last2=Li | first2=Zhibo | last3=Simone | first3=Peter | last4=Lodge | first4=Timothy P. | title=Self-Assembly of Block Copolymer Micelles in an Ionic Liquid | journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society | publisher=American Chemical Society (ACS) | volume=128 | issue=8 | year=2006 | issn=0002-7863 | doi=10.1021/ja058091t | pages=2745–2750| pmid=16492063 | bibcode=2006JAChS.128.2745H }}</ref>  Ionic liquids are considered by many to be "green" solvents due to their vanishing [[vapor pressure]], [[Fireproofing|fire resistance]], as well as their excellent chemical and thermal stability over wide temperature ranges. Besides elucidating the assembly properties of block copolymers in ionic liquids, Lodge has used these materials to produce [[molecular shuttle]]s,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=He | first1=Yiyong | last2=Lodge | first2=Timothy P. | title=The Micellar Shuttle: Thermoreversible, Intact Transfer of Block Copolymer Micelles between an Ionic Liquid and Water | journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society | publisher=American Chemical Society (ACS) | volume=128 | issue=39 | year=2006 | issn=0002-7863 | doi=10.1021/ja0655587 | pages=12666–12667| pmid=17002358 | bibcode=2006JAChS.12812666H }}</ref> gas separation membranes,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Gu | first1=Yuanyan | last2=Lodge | first2=Timothy P. | title=Synthesis and Gas Separation Performance of Triblock Copolymer Ion Gels with a Polymerized Ionic Liquid Mid-Block | journal=Macromolecules | publisher=American Chemical Society (ACS) | volume=44 | issue=7 | date=2011-04-12 | issn=0024-9297 | doi=10.1021/ma2001838 | pages=1732–1736| bibcode=2011MaMol..44.1732G }}</ref> and ion gel gate dielectrics for use in polymer thin film transistors.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Cho | first1=J. H. | last2=Lee | first2=J. | last3=He | first3=Y. | last4=Kim | first4=B. S. | last5=Lodge | first5=T. P. | last6=Frisbie | first6=C. D. | title=High-Capacitance Ion Gel Gate Dielectrics with Faster Polarization Response Times for Organic Thin Film Transistors | journal=Advanced Materials | publisher=Wiley | volume=20 | issue=4 | date=2008-02-18 | issn=0935-9648 | doi=10.1002/adma.200701069 | pages=686–690| bibcode=2008AdM....20..686C | s2cid=95210522 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Cho | first1=Jeong Ho | last2=Lee | first2=Jiyoul | last3=Xia | first3=Yu | last4=Kim | first4=BongSoo | last5=He | first5=Yiyong | last6=Renn | first6=Michael J. | last7=Lodge | first7=Timothy P. | last8=Daniel Frisbie | first8=C. | title=Printable ion-gel gate dielectrics for low-voltage polymer thin-film transistors on plastic | journal=Nature Materials | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=7 | issue=11 | date=2008-10-19 | issn=1476-1122 | doi=10.1038/nmat2291 | pages=900–906| pmid=18931674 | bibcode=2008NatMa...7..900C }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Lee | first1=Jiyoul | last2=Panzer | first2=Matthew J. | last3=He | first3=Yiyong | last4=Lodge | first4=Timothy P. | last5=Frisbie | first5=C. Daniel | title=Ion Gel Gated Polymer Thin-Film Transistors | journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society | publisher=American Chemical Society (ACS) | volume=129 | issue=15 | year=2007 | issn=0002-7863 | doi=10.1021/ja070875e | pages=4532–4533| pmid=17381097 | bibcode=2007JAChS.129.4532L }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=He | first1=Yiyong | last2=Boswell | first2=Paul G. | last3=Bühlmann | first3=Philippe | last4=Lodge | first4=Timothy P. | title=Ion Gels by Self-Assembly of a Triblock Copolymer in an Ionic Liquid† | journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry B | publisher=American Chemical Society (ACS) | volume=111 | issue=18 | year=2007 | issn=1520-6106 | doi=10.1021/jp064574n | pages=4645–4652| pmid=17474692 }}</ref>

'''Education in Polymer Science:''' Lodge is a co-author of ''Polymer Chemistry, 2nd Edition'', written with Paul Hiemenz (2007).  In 2012 he was elected to the University of Minnesota Academy of Distinguished Teachers, and he received the Postbaccalaureate, Graduate, and Professional Education Award.

Lodge is the co-holder of four [[patent]]s.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://patents.justia.com/inventor/timothy-p-lodge | title=Patents by Inventor Timothy P. Lodge | publisher=Justia | access-date=7 November 2015}}</ref>

==Awards, honors, and professional service==
For his research and education efforts, Lodge has received numerous awards including:

*1993           Institute of Technology George Taylor Distinguished Research Award<ref name="TLCEMS"/>
*1993		Fellow of the American Physical Society<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm |title=APS Fellow Archive |publisher=Aps.org |date=2013-04-16 |access-date=2015-03-10}}</ref>
*1994, 2002	National Science Foundation Special Creativity Award<ref name="TLCEMS">{{cite web | url=https://www.cems.umn.edu/people/faculty/timothy-lodge | title=Tim Lodge Regents Professor | publisher=Regents of the University of Minnesota | access-date=7 November 2015}}</ref>
*1994           Fellow of the Humphrey Institute Policy Forum, 1994-95<ref name="TLCEMS"/>
*1998		Arthur K. Doolittle Award, American Chemical Society<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pmse.sites.acs.org/dolittleaward.htm |title=Arthur K. Dolittle Award - Polymeric Materials: Science and Engineering Division |publisher=Pmse.sites.acs.org |date= |access-date=2015-03-10}}</ref>
*1999           EPSRC Visiting Fellow, University of Leeds<ref name="TLCEMS"/>
*2004		American Physical Society Polymer Physics Prize<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Lodge&first_nm=Timothy&year=2004 |title=Prize Recipient |publisher=Aps.org |date=2013-04-16 |access-date=2015-03-10}}</ref>
*2004		Paul Flory Polymer Research Award, POLYCHAR<ref>{{cite web|url=http://iupac.org/publications/ci/2004/2604/cc2_060104.html |title=Chemistry International - Newsmagazine for IUPAC |publisher=Iupac.org |date= |access-date=2015-03-10}}</ref>
*2007           Nelson W. Taylor Award in Materials Science, Penn State University<ref name="TLCEMS"/> 
*2007–2011 	Lloyd H. Reyerson Professor of Chemistry<ref>{{cite web | url=http://pubs.acs.org/page/amlccd/profile.html| title=Editor Profile ACS Publications | publisher=ACS Publications | access-date=7 November 2015}}</ref>
*2009		Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science<ref>{{cite web |url=http://membercentral.aaas.org/fellows |title=Fellows &#124; AAAS MemberCentral |publisher=Membercentral.aaas.org |access-date=2015-03-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140727124856/http://membercentral.aaas.org/fellows |archive-date=2014-07-27 }}</ref>
*2009		International Scientist Award, Society of Polymer Science Japan<ref name="TLCEMS"/>
*2010		Award in Polymer Chemistry, American Chemical Society<ref>{{cite web |url=http://webapps.acs.org/findawards/detail.jsp?ContentId=CTP_004544 |title=American Chemical Society |publisher=Webapps.acs.org |access-date=2015-03-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141211112956/http://webapps.acs.org/findawards/detail.jsp?ContentId=CTP_004544 |archive-date=2014-12-11 }}</ref>
*2010		Fellow of the American Chemical Society<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cen.acs.org/articles/88/i31/2010-ACS-Fellows.html |title=2010 ACS Fellows &#124; August 2, 2010 Issue - Vol. 88 Issue 31 &#124; Chemical & Engineering News |publisher=Cen.acs.org |date=2010-08-02 |access-date=2015-03-10}}</ref>
*2012		Elected to University of Minnesota Academy of Distinguished Teachers<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.adt.umn.edu/about/documents/UpdatedADTList-UpdatedMarch2013.pdf |title=Membership of the Academy of Distinguished Teachers |publisher=Adt.umn.edu |access-date=2015-03-10}}</ref>
*2015           Herman F. Mark Award<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.polyacs.org/1155.html | title=2015 Herman F. Mark Award Winner: Timothy P. Lodge | publisher=American Chemical Society | access-date=7 November 2015}}</ref>
*2016           Elected to American Academy of Arts and Sciences<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.amacad.org/content/news/pressReleases.aspx?pr=10257 | title=Press Releases - American Academy of Arts & Sciences}}</ref>

Lodge has been a Visiting Professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara (1991-2, Chemical Engineering), University of Mainz, Germany (1998, Institute for Physical Chemistry) and Kyoto University (1985; 1992; 1994, Department of Polymer Chemistry)

Since 2005, Lodge has been the director of the NSF-funded Materials Research Science and Engineering Center at Minnesota.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://cse.umn.edu/admin/comm/features/2005_12_LODGE_TO_LEAD_MATERIAL.php |title=Lodge to lead Materials Research Science and Engineering Center (MRSEC) : College of Science & Engineering: University of Minnesota, Twin Cities |publisher=Cse.umn.edu |access-date=2015-03-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402153514/http://cse.umn.edu/admin/comm/features/2005_12_LODGE_TO_LEAD_MATERIAL.php |archive-date=2015-04-02 }}</ref>  The Center currently focuses on materials development in: (1) Engineered Multiblock Polymers, (2) Organic [[Optoelectronics|Optoelectronic]] Interfaces, (3) Magnetic [[Heterojunction|Heterostructures]], and (4) [[Nanoparticle]]-based Materials.

Lodge has served the broader scientific community as the Editor-in-Chief for the American Chemical Society journals ''Macromolecules'' and ''ACS Macro Letters''.  He has served as Chair Elect, Vice Chair, Chair (1995-1998) and Councilor (2001-2006) for the American Physical Society Division of Polymer Physics.<ref name="CFP"/>
